The proof of the theorem `lg_target` hinges on understanding the relationship between the order structure of the ring $ R $ and the image of the strictly monotonic ring homomorphism $ f : R \to S $. The key lies in translating the inequality between two Archimedean classes in $ S $, defined using absolute values, back to a condition on elements of $ R $ via $ f $.

Since $ f $ is strictly monotonic, it preserves the order structure, and we can use this to relate inequalities in $ S $ to inequalities in $ R $. The goal is to show that $ \text{ArchimedeanClass.mk } x \leq \text{ArchimedeanClass.mk } y $ if and only if there exists some $ q \in R $ such that $ 0 < f(q) $ and $ f(q) \cdot |y| \leq |x| $. 

This involves:

1. Using the definition of `ArchimedeanClass.mk_le_mk` which states that $ \text{ArchimedeanClass.mk } a \leq \text{ArchimedeanClass.mk } b $ iff there exists an integer multiple $ n $ such that $ |b| \leq n \cdot |a| $.
2. Translating this into the context of the image of $ f $, leveraging the strict monotonicity of $ f $ to relate $ |x| $ and $ |y| $ to elements of $ R $.
3. Applying the Archimedean property of $ R $ to ensure that for any positive element $ f(q) $, we can find a sufficiently large $ q $ such that the required inequality holds.

By carefully analyzing the order-theoretic properties of $ f $ and the Archimedean structure of $ R $, we can establish the equivalence stated in the theorem.
